page: Amazon Web Services m8id.metal-48xl is a bare-metal server type belonging to the general-purpose family, utilizing the x86_64 instruction set architecture. It is powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 6975P-C processors running at frequencies up to 3.9 GHz, featuring 96 physical cores and 192 virtual CPUs via simultaneous multithreading. The processor configuration is equipped with 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 480 MB L3 cache pool. Architectural extensions include Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions) and AVX-512 variants, providing specialized vector and matrix instruction capability directly on bare metal without hypervisor mediation.

System memory consists of 768 GB of DDR5 RAM operating at 7 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio with 4.0 GB of memory per core. Storage is provided through 11,400 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD instance store volumes, delivering high-throughput, low-latency I/O directly attached to the platform. The server does not bundle dedicated graphics processing units. Network interfaces provide a baseline bandwidth of 75 Gbps, though no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default.

Benchmark evaluations indicate exceptional multi-core scalability and memory throughput. The server achieved 209,047.92 in stress-ng multi-core tests and a PassMark CPU score of 145,286.06, placing it in the top decile of tested systems. Memory bandwidth is measured at 598.83 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and 242.29 GB/sec for writes. The platform also registered 262.57 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations and high Clang compilation throughput, driven by its 192 dedicated execution threads.

Given the dense core count, fast DDR5 channels, and expansive local NVMe disk array, the instance offers strong hardware resource density for high-throughput operational tasks. The primary operational tradeoff involves the ephemeral nature of the bundled local NVMe storage, requiring application-level data redundancy. The system is well structured for large-scale relational and non-relational database clusters, in-memory caching layers, extensive software compilation pipelines, and multi-threaded ETL jobs.

The system includes 768 GB of DDR5 memory at 7 GHz, delivering a standard 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio, alongside 11,400 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD instance storage. Networking capacity reaches a baseline of 75 Gbps without hypervisor overhead. In benchmarks, the instance demonstrates top-tier multi-threaded processing, scoring high across stress-ng, PassMark database operations, and Redis throughput exceeding 262 million operations per second. With dense execution threads and high memory bandwidth, it is suited for high-concurrency databases, large-scale caching, parallel build pipelines, and enterprise backend applications.
